analysis: Examined the three modified ProviderCore files. ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift changed only a comment (lines 70-71); its behavior is unchanged (proactiveReclaimSweep, capacity reporting, prefix cache snapshot). ProviderLoop+MemoryProtection.swift adds CBv2RetainedKVSegments.requestRelease() before MLX.Memory.clearCache() (head lines 59-60), inside the existing nativeProcessAllowsReclamation / MiMo fault guards. This only signals engines to drop free KV segments at their next step; it adds no new data egress, key handling, or persistence. Releasing free KV memory is neutral or positive for T-028 (residual data in GPU memory), and it touches no SSD-tier surface from T-041 (HMAC names, TTL, DBK3 crypto, salt scoping). ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift (patch only, excerpt truncated) reworks eviction and admission accounting. Retained KV segment bytes now count as reclaim credit only before a release (countingRetainedKVSegments), and a new releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad() runs before evicting. fastAdmissionReject now awaits nemotronSuperLoadIsCertainToFail and re-checks the refusal verdicts after the suspension. This is memory accounting and availability logic, and I saw no authorization, attestation, encryption, or billing paths affected. Residual availability risk: the eviction loop's `continue` after the first poolDropped release is bounded because poolDropped is set once. Unverified, outside the supplied evidence: the implementations of CBv2RetainedKVSegments and GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments, and the truncated remainder of the ModelLoading patch. No concrete regression identified against the threat model.
